scenarios.title: A spell that produces mana adds it to the caster's pool when it resolves
decisions: A casts Dark Ritual, tapping Swamp for {B}.
B passes priority; Dark Ritual resolves (unless a variant says otherwise).
A casts Black Knight, paying {B}{B} from the mana pool if the pool holds mana.
B passes priority; the cast Black Knight resolves.

variants.label: base
variants.expected: Dark Ritual resolves and A's mana pool holds {B}{B}{B}. A pays {B}{B} for Black Knight from the pool, one {B} stays in the pool, and Black Knight resolves onto A's battlefield.

variants.label: ritual_countered
variants.delta: B responds to Dark Ritual by casting Counterspell (tapping both Islands) targeting it.
variants.expected: Dark Ritual is countered and moves to A's graveyard without resolving. A's mana pool stays empty, Black Knight cannot be cast and stays in A's hand.

operation.unclassifiable: a different spell cast: B casts a counterspell in response

detector.outcome: A spell's or ability's effect adds mana: the record holds a mana_produced event naming the player who gets it.
detector.near_miss: No near miss is counted: mana production is written by the mana hook as its own record, so a Mana resolution's bracketed half holding none would be a false near miss.

scenarios.title: A land's mana ability adds mana to its controller's pool
decisions: A activates the mana ability of Forest (tapping it for {G}) to pay for Llanowar Elves and attempts to cast Llanowar Elves.

variants.label: base
variants.expected: Legal: the mana ability adds {G} to A's pool, A casts Llanowar Elves, and it resolves onto A's battlefield.

variants.label: forest_tapped
variants.expected: Not legal: the mana ability cannot be activated, no mana is added to A's pool, and Llanowar Elves cannot be cast.

detector.outcome: A candidate is affordable: the player's untapped mana sources can add the mana its cost needs.
detector.near_miss: A candidate that is not affordable for want of mana a source can add.

scenarios.title: Unspent mana is lost when the step ends

setup.notes: A has no source of mana besides Mountain.

decisions: A taps Mountain for {R}, which stays in A's mana pool, without casting anything.
A and B pass priority with an empty stack; the game moves to the beginning of combat step.
In the beginning of combat step A receives priority and attempts to cast Shock targeting B.

variants.label: base
variants.expected: Not legal: the {R} was lost when main phase 1 ended, A's mana pool is empty and Mountain is tapped, so Shock cannot be cast. B stays at 20 life.

variants.label: cast_in_same_step
variants.delta: A casts Shock targeting B in main phase 1, right after tapping Mountain, paying with the {R} still in the pool.
variants.expected: Legal: the {R} is still in the pool, Shock is cast and resolves, and B goes to 18 life.

operation.unclassifiable: a different decision: A casts the spell in the same step instead of passing

scenarios.title: A mana ability that would produce mana of an undefined color produces no mana

setup.notes: Meteor Crater is a colorless land, so A controls no colored permanent.

decisions: A activates Meteor Crater's mana ability, choosing green if a color is available, and attempts to cast Llanowar Elves with the mana.

variants.label: base
variants.expected: Not legal: A controls no colored permanent, so the ability produces no mana, A's pool stays empty and Llanowar Elves cannot be cast. Meteor Crater is tapped.

variants.label: colorless_artifact
variants.delta: A also controls Sol Ring, a colorless artifact.
variants.expected: Not legal: Sol Ring is colorless too, so the ability still produces no mana and Llanowar Elves cannot be cast.

operation.unclassifiable: adds a permanent (a colourless artifact) to A's battlefield

variants.label: green_permanent
variants.delta: A also controls Grizzly Bears, a green creature.
variants.expected: Legal: Meteor Crater adds {G} (the color of Grizzly Bears), A casts Llanowar Elves, and it resolves onto A's battlefield.

operation.unclassifiable: adds a permanent (a green creature) to A's battlefield

scenarios.forge_notes: Grizzly Bears and Sol Ring are on the battlefield only in the variant that names them.

detector.none: A mana ability that produces no mana is written nowhere: ManaChannel returns without a record when the produced string is empty, so no mana_produced and no resolution record exists; the snapshot's untapped_production is a per-player total by colour that names no source; a decision candidate's affordable=false does not say which source failed or why.

scenarios.title: Restricted mana can be spent only on what its restriction allows

setup.notes: Ancient Ziggurat is A's only mana source. Its mana can be spent only to cast creature spells.

decisions: A activates Ancient Ziggurat's mana ability, choosing red, and attempts to cast Shock targeting B with that mana.

variants.label: base
variants.expected: Not legal: the {R} can be spent only on a creature spell, so Shock cannot be cast with it. B stays at 20 life.

variants.label: creature_spell
variants.delta: A attempts to cast Raging Goblin (a red creature spell) instead of Shock.
variants.expected: Legal: the {R} may be spent on a creature spell, Raging Goblin is cast and resolves onto A's battlefield. B stays at 20 life.

operation.unclassifiable: a different spell cast: A tries a creature spell instead

scenarios.title: Spending restricted mana can give the spell an additional effect

setup.notes: Cavern of Souls entered with the creature type Human chosen. Elite Vanguard is a Human Soldier.

decisions: A casts Elite Vanguard, paying {W} with Cavern of Souls (its colored-mana ability, choosing white).
B responds by casting Counterspell targeting Elite Vanguard, tapping both Islands.
Both players pass; Counterspell resolves, then the creature spell, if still on the stack, resolves.

variants.label: base
variants.expected: Elite Vanguard can't be countered because mana from Cavern of Souls was spent on it: Counterspell resolves without countering it, Counterspell goes to B's graveyard, and Elite Vanguard (2/1) enters A's battlefield.

variants.label: paid_with_plains
variants.delta: A pays {W} with Plains instead of Cavern of Souls.
variants.expected: No restricted mana was spent, so Counterspell counters Elite Vanguard: both Elite Vanguard and Counterspell move to their owners' graveyards.

operation.unclassifiable: a different payment decision: A pays with another land

scenarios.forge_notes: The creature type chosen as Cavern of Souls enters must be set to Human in the setup.

detector.none: The rider spent mana gives a spell is in no record field: a resolution's costs record mana_by_color with no restriction or rider, floating_mana carries none, and a Counter resolution without spell_countered shows only that the spell was not countered, not that spent mana made it so.

scenarios.title: A mana-doubling replacement effect gives every added mana the source's restriction

setup.notes: Ancient Ziggurat is A's only mana source. Mana Reflection doubles the mana produced when A taps a permanent for mana.

decisions: A activates Ancient Ziggurat's mana ability, choosing white; with Mana Reflection it adds {W}{W}.
A casts the first Elite Vanguard, paying with one {W}; it resolves.
A then attempts to cast Healing Salve with the remaining {W}, choosing the mode 'target player gains 3 life' and targeting A.

variants.label: base
variants.expected: The first Elite Vanguard is legal and resolves. Healing Salve is not legal: the second {W} also can be spent only on a creature spell, so it cannot pay for Healing Salve. A stays at 20 life.

variants.label: second_creature
variants.delta: A attempts to cast the second Elite Vanguard instead of Healing Salve.
variants.expected: Legal: the second {W} is restricted to creature spells and Elite Vanguard is a creature spell, so both Elite Vanguards resolve onto A's battlefield.

operation.unclassifiable: a different spell cast: A tries a creature spell instead

variants.label: unrestricted_source
variants.delta: A's land is Plains instead of Ancient Ziggurat.
variants.expected: Legal: Mana Reflection makes Plains add {W}{W} with no restriction, both Elite Vanguard and Healing Salve are cast and resolve, and A goes to 23 life.

scenarios.forge_notes: Plains is on the battlefield only in the variant that names it.

scenarios.title: A land that copies what an opponent's lands could produce yields only those types
decisions: A activates Exotic Orchard's mana ability, choosing green if a color is available, and attempts to cast Llanowar Elves with the mana.

variants.label: base
variants.expected: Legal: B's Forest could produce {G}, so Exotic Orchard adds {G}, A casts Llanowar Elves, and it resolves onto A's battlefield.

variants.label: opponent_mountain
variants.delta: B's land is Mountain instead of Forest.
variants.expected: Not legal: Exotic Orchard can add only {R}, so {G} is not available and Llanowar Elves cannot be cast.

variants.label: opponent_no_lands
variants.expected: Not legal: no type of mana is defined, Exotic Orchard produces no mana, and Llanowar Elves cannot be cast.

scenarios.forge_notes: Forest and Mountain are on B's battlefield only in the variants that name them.

scenarios.title: A trigger for permanents tapped for a type of mana fires only when that mana is produced by tapping

setup.notes: Llanowar Elves has been under A's control since before the turn began. Forsaken Monument reads: whenever you tap a permanent for {C}, add an additional {C}.

decisions: A activates Sol Ring's mana ability, tapping it for {C}{C}.
No other action is taken; A's mana pool is read after the mana ability has resolved.

variants.label: base
variants.expected: Forsaken Monument's trigger fires because Sol Ring was tapped for {C}; A's pool holds {C}{C}{C}.

variants.label: tapped_for_green
variants.delta: A taps Llanowar Elves for {G} instead of Sol Ring.
variants.expected: The trigger does not fire because the permanent was tapped for {G}, not {C}; A's pool holds only {G}.

operation.unclassifiable: a different decision: A activates another permanent's mana ability

variants.label: no_tap_cost
variants.delta: A sacrifices Llanowar Elves to Ashnod's Altar for {C}{C} instead of tapping Sol Ring.
variants.expected: The trigger does not fire because Ashnod's Altar's ability has no {T} in its cost, so no permanent was tapped for mana; A's pool holds only {C}{C}.

operation.unclassifiable: a different decision: A activates a sacrifice mana ability instead

scenarios.forge_notes: Forsaken Monument also pumps colorless creatures and gains life on colorless spells; nothing in the scenario is colorless creature or cast.

detector.outcome: A TapsForMana trigger evaluated against a permanent tapped for mana of the type it names fires.
detector.near_miss: A TapsForMana trigger evaluated against mana of another type, or mana produced without tapping, does not fire.

scenarios.title: A replacement effect for permanents tapped for mana changes the mana produced

setup.notes: Llanowar Elves has been under A's control since before the turn began.

decisions: A activates Forest's mana ability, tapping it for {G}.
A casts Grizzly Bears, paying {1}{G} from the mana pool if the pool holds that much; Grizzly Bears resolves.

variants.label: base
variants.expected: Mana Reflection replaces the production: Forest adds {G}{G} instead of {G}. A pays {1}{G} for Grizzly Bears and it resolves onto A's battlefield.

variants.label: no_tap_cost
variants.delta: A sacrifices Llanowar Elves to Ashnod's Altar for {C}{C} instead of tapping Forest.
variants.expected: Mana Reflection does not apply because nothing was tapped for mana: A's pool holds exactly {C}{C} (not four), and Grizzly Bears cannot be cast because no {G} is available.

operation.unclassifiable: a different decision: A activates a sacrifice mana ability instead

scenarios.forge_notes: Forge's Mana Reflection script (Event$ ProduceMana, ValidCard$ Permanent) does not check for a tap cost, so Forge may double Ashnod's Altar's mana; the expected outcome follows the rule text.

detector.outcome: A mana production event met by a replacement for permanents tapped for mana is modified in place (ReplaceMana reports Updated).
detector.near_miss: A mana production event that met such a replacement and was not modified.

scenarios.title: Drain Power moves the other player's unspent mana to its caster, restrictions intact

setup.notes: A's lands are only the two Islands; A has no way to produce {R} itself.

decisions: A casts Drain Power targeting B, tapping both Islands.
B passes priority; Drain Power resolves: B activates the mana ability of each land B controls, choosing red where there is a choice, then B loses all unspent mana and A adds the mana lost this way.
A attempts to cast Shock targeting B with the mana in A's pool.

variants.label: base
variants.expected: B's Mountain is tapped for {R}, B's pool is emptied and A's pool gets {R}. Shock is cast with it and resolves: B goes to 18 life.

variants.label: no_mana
variants.expected: B has no unspent mana to lose, so A adds nothing. Shock cannot be cast, and B stays at 20 life.

variants.label: restricted_mana
variants.delta: B's land is Ancient Ziggurat instead of Mountain, tapped for {R}.
variants.expected: A's pool gets {R} that can be spent only on a creature spell, so Shock cannot be cast with it. B stays at 20 life.

scenarios.forge_notes: Forge's Drain Power script first makes the target player activate a mana ability of each land they control, matching the current Oracle text, so B's untapped land always produces mana; the no_mana variant relies on B's land being tapped.

detector.none: Draining mana is written in no record field: DrainManaEffect clears one pool and calls ManaPool.addMana on the other, bypassing the mana hook (AbilityManaPart.produceMana) that alone writes mana_produced; mana_lost is written only on a LoseMana replacement's rewrite record; the acting line's root API is ActivateAbility; and the resolution's snapshot precedes the drain.
